newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Marines evacuate 1,217 from Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Marines evacuate 1,217 from Sierra Leone.

text.p: U.S. Marines using helicopters on Tuesday evacuated another 1,217 foreigners, including about 20 Americans, from the troubled capital of Sierra Leone, the Defence Department said.

"There have been no casualties. It has been a well-run operation. They are all out, off the beach now," Defence Secretary William Cohen told reporters after the Marines completed their third round of evacuations since Friday to the U.S. warship Kearsarge.

Tuesday's evacuation from Freetown, where the Army recently ousted Sierra Leone's elected leaders in a military coup, brought to nearly 2,500 the total number of persons, including some 430 Americans, removed since Friday.

"The final number (on Tuesday) is 1,217 and all of the Marines are off the beach," said Marine Corps Lt. Gen. James Jones, Cohen's senior military aide, as Cohen spoke briefly with reporters after a picture session with visiting Slovenian Defense Minister Tit Turnsek.
Defense officials said Tuesday's evacuees were removed from a breachfront near a restaurant because a hotel earlier used as an evacuation point was too dangerous.
